description: A lightweight .NET library for internal JWT authentication and claims handling, with refresh token rotation, password hashing, TOTP primitives, WebAuthn/FIDO2 second-factor and passkey sign-in verification, query-string tokens for WebSocket connections, path-scoped cookie tokens for files opened in a new tab, and an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for MCP clients with app-owned consent
releaseNotes: An OAuth 2.1 authorization server, opt-in: AddEasyReasyOAuthServer and AddOAuthServerEndpoints serve RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 discovery (with a 401 challenge naming the protected resource metadata), dynamic client registration and client ID metadata documents fetched only from public addresses, the authorization code flow with PKCE S256 only, refresh tokens rotated with reuse detection, and RFC 7009 revocation. Your consent page approves through IOAuthGrantHandler, which records the grant and decides the claims at approval and on every refresh; only a person signed in to your app can approve, and the handler is given the request id, so it can make a repeated approval idempotent. You implement IOAuthServerStore, kept apart from IRefreshTokenStore, and end a connection with IOAuthGrantService.RevokeGrantAsync. Client tokens are the library's own JWTs carrying client_id (EasyReasyClaimTypes.ClientId, GetOAuthClientId), issued for the resource as their audience and signed with a separate key derived from your secret. A bearer scheme of their own validates them, and only endpoints opened to connections with [AllowOAuthClients] or .AllowOAuthClients() run it; your app's own bearer cannot validate one, whatever its configuration. An opened endpoint authenticates with exactly your JWT bearer and that scheme, and requires a signed-in caller unless it has authorization of its own; without the server, it refuses every connection token. AddEasyReasyAuth now rejects a JWT secret under 32 bytes when it is called, where before it failed on the first token issued. IRefreshTokenStore now extends IRefreshTokenRotationStore, which holds the four operations rotation needs; a store implementing them as public members compiles unchanged, and one implementing them explicitly names IRefreshTokenRotationStore instead. IAuthAuditLogger gains four defaulted OAuth hooks, and EasyReasyAuthTypes names the "user" and "apikey" auth types. Behaviour change for every app, with or without the server: a refresh that theft detection, a logout or a revocation lands in the middle of now fails with TokenInvalidated and gives its new refresh token up, where before that token outlived the invalidation; this needs IRefreshTokenStore.InvalidateFamilyAsync to mark consumed tokens too. See https://github.com/AdamTovatt/easy-reasy/blob/auth-v5.17.0/EasyReasy.Auth/README.md#migration-from-5160
title: EasyReasy.Auth
